implementation_notes: There is nothing to hand-wrap for OS and network APIs: Node's fs and net modules are the wrapper facade over libuv and the underlying syscalls, fs.promises.open returns a FileHandle that owns the descriptor and implements disposal, and net.Socket owns the connection. The work is to use those types rather than re-expose them, and to add a facade only when the API is a third-party native library (see the Node-API variant) or when the domain deserves a type with invariants - a protocol session, for example. ES2017 is the floor because async/await is what makes the promise-based wrappers usable as ordinary sequential code.
pitfalls: fs and crypto work runs on the libuv thread pool: a facade that fires many of these calls at once queues behind a handful of threads instead of scaling.
Handles are not reclaimed deterministically - an unclosed FileHandle or socket keeps the event loop alive and leaks a descriptor.
Reaching for handle.fd escapes the facade's lifetime rules and lets callers use a descriptor the facade will close.

variants.name: Node-API native addon wrapping a C library
variants.idiom_name: node-addon-api class owning the C handle
variants.implementation_notes: When the non-OO API is a C library without a JavaScript binding, the facade is a native addon built on Node-API: a C++ class owns the native handle, exposes intent-named methods to JavaScript, and frees the handle when the wrapper object is finalized. Node-API is the ABI-stable C surface maintained inside Node.js, so a binding built against it does not have to be recompiled for each Node major version, and the JavaScript side can stay a thin typed module.
pitfalls: A blocking C call in an addon method stalls the event loop; use AsyncWorker or a thread-safe function instead of calling it directly.
Addons must clean up on environment shutdown (napi_add_env_cleanup_hook) and must not cache a napi_env across worker threads.
Native addons need a toolchain and per-platform prebuilds at install time, which is a real distribution cost the JavaScript-only path does not have.
